html:
The Guatemalan Civil War was fought from 1960 to 1996 between the army governments of Guatemala and left-wing guerrillas. About 200,000 people were killed or disappeared, most of them Maya civilians killed by the army.

Its roots lay in the coup of 1954, organised by the CIA, which overthrew President Jacobo Árbenz after his land reform took unused land from the United Fruit Company. In 1960 a group of junior officers revolted, and survivors formed the first guerrilla bands. Through the Cold War the United States mostly backed the army.

The worst years were 1981 to 1983. To cut the guerrillas off from support in the Maya highlands, the army burned hundreds of villages and massacred their people. Q'anjob'al, Tz'utujil, Achi, Ixil and K'iche' communities suffered most, and many survivors fled to Mexico.

A truth commission set up by the peace process found the army responsible for most of the killing and judged some of it genocide against Maya peoples. Rigoberta Menchú, a K'iche' woman who lost much of her family in the war, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992. Peace accords were signed in December 1996.
sum: The Guatemalan Civil War was fought from 1960 to 1996 between the army governments of Guatemala and left-wing guerrillas. About 200,000 people were killed or disappeared, most of them Maya civilians killed by the army.
